title: One index file over several data files
body:
An `Index` describes one file. `Index::write` stamps that file's length and mtime into the header, and the free function `is_current` re-stats one data path against one index path. `Aggregate<IndexedFasta>` numbers several indexed files as one range. Nothing on disk records which files were aggregated or in which order. The numbering exists only in the call that built it.

This milestone adds an atlas: a `.satlas` file listing the parts in order, with a stamp and a record count for each, pointing at each part's own `.saidx`. One read of it gives the total and each part's first position. `sail index` stays the command for one file. `sail atlas` writes an atlas over several, and every subcommand reads an atlas as one input.

The pieces:

- sail-9d931d decided the atlas points at per-file `.saidx` files.
- sail-978552 decided a stale part is refused and named.
- sail-f5a79d dissolved once the atlas became its own file.
- sail-a59d6f is `libsail::atlas::Atlas` and its file.
- sail-2413e6 is the `sail atlas` command.
- sail-3a486e decides how `Readers` and `Aggregate` are built from an atlas.
- sail-4d86c8 has every subcommand read an atlas as one input.

Alignment of the `.saidx` layout (sail-bb932e) left this milestone. It can be explained without the atlas.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/c45d6630
notes.text: This milestone was 'Selection over a stream and over several files, and an index that spans files' and mixed streaming with the index-file work. Streaming (sail-317db4), the multi-file Reader (sail-0705fb) and its decision (sail-a5d666) now stand alone. Alignment (sail-bb932e) left later for the same reason.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/424f83e5
notes.text:
`Atlas` and `sail atlas` are behind `#[cfg(sail_unstable)]` (sail-917c42), so their changelog entries came out of `[Unreleased]`. Put them back when the gate comes off.

For `libsail`, under `### Added`:

```text
- `atlas::Atlas`, an ordered list of data files kept in a `.satlas`
  file of its own. `build(paths, format)` writes a named `.saidx` beside each
  path that lacks a current one and reuses the rest. The atlas stamps each
  data file and records its count, so `starts()` and `stale()` open no index
  file. Parts are stored relative to the atlas's directory, so the two can
  move together.
```

For `sail`, under `### Added`, without the last sentence once sail-4d86c8 lands:

```text
- `atlas`, which writes a `.saidx` beside each of several files, then a
  `.satlas` file at `-o` listing them in order with each file's record count.
  It reuses a current index and rebuilds a missing or stale one. Every input
  must be the same format. No command reads an atlas yet.
```

The README's command count goes from twenty to twenty-one.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/424f83e5
notes.text: The atlas work lives on the `atlas` branch, per CLAUDE.md's Branches rule: `Atlas` and `sail atlas` are there, and sail-3a486e and sail-4d86c8 go there too. The branch merges into `dev` once the milestone is whole.
